notes.content: A typed letter opening Dear Murre criticizes the recipient's notes on the tame fundamental group. Paragraph 2 gives an example attached to 1.16 and 3.6 and traces consequences for proofs of 3.7 and 3.8. Paragraph 3 disputes 6.4 without regularity of the D_i and proposes a normal-crossings formulation using étale-local irreductible components. These statements are reported as the author's claims, not independently established results. The page has three body paragraphs, no heading/date/signature, no standalone display, no diagram, and no free-standing drawing. The only non-textual stroke is an inline punctuation addition; the bottom-left 7 is archival.
author_checks: “I did not try to check 3.8. by some different proof”.
titles_dates_pages: No title, date, signature or visible authorial/typed page number.
Pale handwritten archival 7 at bottom-left; represented as % archive sheet number: 7.
math_reading_decisions: All primes, both superscript n marks, each equality, the minus sign, the slash and parentheses in the polynomial expression were checked against half a.
The three unmarked arrow slots and missing brackets were preserved as visible spacing. H's editorial note is not manuscript text and its mathematical restoration of arrows was not adopted.
Both D_i occurrences were read independently as D with subscript i from half b.
The numeral values 3.6, 3.7 and 3.8 twice are certain; their type/hand state remains locally qualified.

A conditional algebraic substitution check was actually performed: if a=b^n, evaluating T^n-a at T=b gives zero. This checks only the relation behind a section; it does not verify the unstated geometric hypotheses or group actions.

The author's assertions about non-surjectivity, failure of 1.16 and 3.6, dependence of the proofs of 3.7/3.8, the correction to 6.4, and the proposed ramification generalization remain unverified background.
notes.visual_audit: The greeting and every line of all three paragraphs, including agreed C/H text, were read against the two supplied halves. The right/below areas of line endings were inspected for detached punctuation. Abbreviations and typographical slips were kept; line-break-only hyphenation in recasting and statement was joined. No OCR, outside source, other page, other reader output, or LaTeX compilation was used.
